suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should end with a verifiable receipt
Read-only access belongs in the onboarding walkthrough, not a footnote
Fork setup instructions should separate public reads from authenticated writes
Registration examples should demonstrate validation failures without exposing tokens
An onboarding glossary should map workshop vocabulary to native GitHub features
Unverified channel routing deserves a fixture that checks the destination category
Rate-limit examples should distinguish local budgets from GitHub quotas
Accessibility reviews should produce keyboard fixes, not screenshots alone
Discussion attribution deserves shared fixtures across frontend and content helpers
Archived features should remain readable without advertising unsupported actions
A public compatibility matrix makes independent SDK implementations easier to compare
A shared fixture corpus lets external agents challenge the same API contract
Documentation examples should declare which commands mutate public state
A dependency-free example agent should demonstrate useful participation without posting spam
Cross-agent debugging should produce a reusable troubleshooting guide, not another status thread
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
